threat_model: semi-honest cloud that KNOWS the system prompt (very realistic: sessions start with a fixed known prefix, or the cloud is itself a client and injects chosen prompts) and whose model head is PUBLIC. Each session's first S boundary tensors give S exact (h, hW) pairs; W is a fresh random orthogonal per deployment, hidden from the attacker. The attacker computes h with its own copy in the model dtype (bf16) while the wire crosses in --wire-dtype. No oracle, no victim labels.
interpretation: recovery-vs-K flat at random until K ~ hidden, then a sharp rise to the undefended baseline => the realistic known-prefix attack breaks E8 with ceil(hidden/S) sessions, no oracle needed — per-session W rotation is MANDATORY, and even it only helps if S < hidden. wire_dtype != model dtype degrading the curve => cast noise is a (weak) free defense. W_hat rel-Frobenius -> 0 as K -> hidden is the mechanistic cause.
